THOUGHT: The clinical picture is of an acute, rapidly progressive, unilateral optic neuropathy with early disc swelling progressing to complete vision loss and combined retinal vascular occlusion. MRI shows an enlarged, contrast-enhancing optic nerve with FLAIR hyperintensity. The decisive data are the vitreous biopsy and immunohistochemistry: tumor cells that are GFAP+ and Olig2+, with mutant IDH1, p53 positivity, ATRX loss, and a modest Ki‑67 (~10%). That immunophenotype (IDH‑mutant, ATRX loss, p53 mutation, GFAP/Olig2 expression) is diagnostic of an astrocytic lineage diffuse glioma (IDH‑mutant astrocytoma). The location and imaging implicate the optic nerve/optic pathway (an adult optic nerve glioma/optic pathway astrocytoma) with intravitreal seeding/extension that produced mechanical/oncologic occlusion of the central retinal and branch vessels (explaining the FA showing absent retinal perfusion) and the whitish tumor fragment in the posterior vitreous. Alternative explanations (immune checkpoint inhibitor–related optic neuritis/vasculitis, optic nerve sheath meningioma, intraocular lymphoma, metastatic carcinoma, VEGF‑inhibitor thromboembolism) are not supported by the tumor immunophenotype or pathology. Therefore the most likely diagnosis is an IDH‑mutant astrocytic tumor of the optic nerve (optic nerve glioma / optic pathway astrocytoma) with intravitreal tumor seeding causing retinal vascular occlusion and acute vision loss.

DIAGNOSIS:
1. Optic nerve glioma (diffuse IDH‑mutant astrocytoma of the optic nerve / optic pathway astrocytoma) with intravitreal seeding causing combined central retinal artery and vein occlusion.
2. Extension/involvement of the optic nerve from an intracranial IDH‑mutant diffuse astrocytoma (optic pathway glioma spreading from chiasm/tract).
3. Higher‑grade astrocytic tumor of the optic nerve (anaplastic astrocytoma / IDH‑mutant progressing toward glioblastoma) with intravitreal dissemination.
4. Immune checkpoint inhibitor–related severe optic neuritis/vasculitis with secondary retinal vascular occlusion (less likely given biopsy/immunohistochemistry).
5. Intraocular/intraorbital lymphoma or metastatic carcinoma causing optic nerve enlargement and vitreous cells (least likely given GFAP/Olig2/IDH1/ATRX/p53 profile).
ground_truth: Glioblastoma (World Health Organization grade IV) with optic nerve invasion and intraocular extension

Case Information:
A woman in her 40s presented with blurred vision in the right eye. She was undergoing treatment with systemic steroids, durvalumab (a PD-L1 inhibitor), and bevacizumab. Ten days after initial presentation, the patient developed sudden vision loss in the right eye.

Physical Examination:
Initial examination: Visual acuity of 20/25 OU. Right eye showed full visual field, right-sided relative afferent pupillary defect, unremarkable anterior segment, and mild swelling of the optic disc. Left eye had normal fundus and visual function. Follow-up examination (after vision loss): Right eye showed no light perception vision, marked swelling of the optic disc, peripapillary retinal hemorrhages, and occlusion of the superior branch artery. Two days later: Combined occlusion of the central retinal artery and vein, and a new collection of whitish material suspended anterior to the optic disc, forming a pocket in the posterior vitreous.

Diagnostic Tests:
- Imaging Studies:    Image Title: MRI at Onset of Vision Loss    Image Description:     - Coronal T1-weighted contrast-enhanced image: Focal enhancement along enlarged right optic nerve    - Axial T1-weighted contrast-enhanced image: Diffuse enlargement of orbital portion of right optic nerve, enhancement of nerve sheath, slight flattening of posterior globe    - Coronal T2-weighted (FLAIR) image: Hyperintensity of right optic nerve  - Laboratory Tests:    - Lumbar puncture showed no abnormalities      - Other Tests:    - Wide-field fluorescein angiography: Showed choroidal flush but complete lack of perfusion of retinal vasculature      - Pathological Examination:    - Vitreous biopsy: Hypercellular sample with astrocytic neoplasm, small to medium-sized cells with scant cytoplasm and oval, pleomorphic, hyperchromatic nuclei    - Immunohistochemistry: Positive for glial fibrillary acid protein, oligodendrocyte transcription factor 2, mutant IDH-1 protein, p53; Loss of ATRX protein; Ki-67 proliferation index ~10%
